ui.articleExcerpt: From a 3-day manual workflow to 2-hour automation. How BrandHub helps marketing teams scale output without adding headcount.

0.caption: From 3 hours down to 15 minutes per post. No filters, no fluff — just our team's actual workflow after 2 months on BrandHub. A whole week of content scheduled in one morning. Not having to stay up late posting anymore feels amazing.

1.caption: Swipe for the before/after of switching from 5 scattered tools to one platform. 3 months, 247 posts, 0 missed deadlines. 'Wrong format' and 'posted at the wrong time' are ancient history now. A team of 4 managing 12 brands at once.

2.caption: This caption was written by AI in 30 seconds — but the real win is it nailed our brand's tone. BrandHub's AI Assistant now gets how we use emoji, our line breaks, even the little quirks we always use. Feels like having an extra copywriter on the team.

0.caption: POV: you just found a tool that automates your entire content calendar across 5 platforms in one click. Content team went from 6 people to 3. My boss stopped asking 'where's the post' every morning.

1.caption: One tool replacing Canva + Google Calendar + Trello + Google Drive + Messenger. Sounds fake but it's real. This is the actual stack our team uses to run 8 clients at once. Who said agencies have to be chaos?

2.caption: Our content team's reaction to getting 5 Tet campaign briefs at once. With BrandHub Calendar we drag-and-drop the whole schedule in 15 minutes instead of 3 hours in Excel like last year. So many people asked how, we made this video.

0.authorRole: Founder & Creative Director, Bloom Digital Agency
0.content: 4 months into running our whole agency on BrandHub, here are the real numbers: 12 clients, 3 content writers, 247 posts/month, 0 missed deadlines. We used to juggle 5 separate tools — Canva for design, Google Sheets for tracking, Trello for task assignment, Drive for approvals, Messenger for feedback. Getting one post from idea to published took 3-4 days. Now it's all in one tab. My favorite part is the approval workflow: clients review posts right on the platform, no more screenshotting a draft into Messenger and 'hey can you approve this real quick.' If you run an agency, you know that feeling.

1.content: Small brand, no dedicated content team. It's just me shooting photos, writing captions, posting, and replying to comments. Before BrandHub, social ate 3-4 hours of my day — now it's 30 minutes. The AI writes captions that actually sound like my brand (I write mostly in Vietnamese, and BrandHub's AI handles it really well, none of that word-for-word translation feel other tools have). The drag-and-drop calendar means I can see my whole week's content at a glance. Online revenue is up 40% in the first two months, not because I got better at this, but because I finally have time to focus on the product instead of being stuck on content.

2.content: Running the Tet 2026 campaign for 5 brands at once with an 8-person team. Without BrandHub, I honestly don't think we'd have survived January. Cross-platform publishing sends one post to 5 channels (FB, IG, TikTok, LinkedIn, X) with a single click. The content calendar gives us a bird's-eye view of every campaign on one screen — we catch double-bookings and duplicate content instantly. Our team's output is up 240%, and review meeting time is down 80%. Measurable ROI: roughly $3,200/month saved on tooling and headcount.

0.content: 6 months after rolling out BrandHub to a 25-person marketing team, we've grown content output by 240% while cutting approval time by 80%. Our old 4-tier review process for a single post averaged 3.2 days — now it's 4 hours. Here's a detailed case study on how we moved from a manual workflow to AI-assisted content operations without compromising brand safety or compliance.
0.articleHeadline: How We Scaled Content Operations 3x Without Adding Headcount — A Unilever Vietnam Case Study

1.content: We spent 3 months evaluating 4 content management platforms (BrandHub, ContentStudio, Loomly, Vista Social) before deciding. Criteria: multi-brand support, AI writing quality, approval workflow, cross-platform publishing, pricing. BrandHub won on 4 of 5. Here's the detailed breakdown of each platform — not sponsored, just our growth team's real experience.
1.articleHeadline: We Evaluated 4 Content Platforms Over 90 Days — Here's Our Scorecard

2.content: Managing content across 6 Southeast Asian markets, each with its own language and brand guidelines, is a problem we face every single day. BrandHub solved our three biggest pain points: (1) a centralized content calendar that lets regional teams see every campaign from Singapore HQ, (2) AI localization that translates and adjusts tone per market in minutes instead of days, (3) region-based approval permissions — market leads approve local content, regional directors approve major campaigns. Results: time-to-market down 65%, content consistency score up from 6.2 to 8.9/10.
2.articleHeadline: Managing Content Across 6 Markets, 6 Languages: Our BrandHub Playbook

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Clear answers about BrandHub's architecture, security, and collaborative workflows.

q1.q: Is there a free tier to get started?
q1.a: Yes! The Starter plan is completely free. You can create 1 workspace, collaborate with up to 5 team members, connect core social channels, and explore full scheduling and drafting workflows.

q2.q: Which social platforms are natively supported?
q2.a: BrandHub integrates natively with 4 official social platforms: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and Threads. Scheduled content is processed asynchronously by our dedicated Publisher microservice.

q3.q: How does AI Trend Crawler & Brand Guidelines enforcement work?
q3.a: BrandHub combines GraphRAG (Neo4j and ChromaDB vector embeddings) with real-time social trend analysis. The AI identifies emerging viral discussions, strictly validates drafts against your Brand Guidelines (voice, tone, forbidden keywords), and runs automated community safety compliance checks.

q4.q: How does collaboration between Agencies and Clients operate?
q4.a: We provide a role-based access control architecture across 6 canonical roles (Guest, Owner, Manager, Creator, Client, Admin): Agency teams (Owner, Manager, Creator) draft and manage multi-channel campaigns, while Clients access a dedicated approval portal to review, comment on drafts, and sign off.

q5.q: How are social credentials and access tokens secured?
q5.a: Our microservices architecture isolates authentication through Spring Cloud Gateway. Social OAuth tokens are encrypted with AES-256 in the database, with Redis token blacklisting and complete workspace tenant isolation.
